section: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - structure, jurisdiction, working; Central Vigilance Commission
subsections: Lokpal Bill history - first introduction, attempts, year passed, Anna Hazare movement
Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

accepted.s: The idea of an Ombudsman originated in which country in 1809?
accepted.x: The Ombudsman institution originated in Sweden in 1809.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the country associated with the origin of an institution.
accepted.sec: Lokpal Bill history - first introduction, attempts, year passed, Anna Hazare movement

accepted.s: Who coined the term ‘Lokpal’?
accepted.x: The word ‘Lokpal’ was coined by Dr. L.M. Singhvi.
accepted.tq: Test the person associated with the exact origin of a term.
accepted.sec: Lokpal Bill history - first introduction, attempts, year passed, Anna Hazare movement

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the history of the Lokpal Bill:
1. The First Lokpal Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha in 1969.
2. The Bill lapsed when the concerned Lok Sabha was dissolved.
3. The Bill was first introduced in the Rajya Sabha in 1968.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the First Lokpal Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya Sabha.
accepted.tq: Separate the House of introduction from the House of passage and identify the wrong House.
accepted.sec: Lokpal Bill history - first introduction, attempts, year passed, Anna Hazare movement

accepted.s: Which one of the following years was NOT among the years in which the Lokpal Bill was re-introduced after 1969?
accepted.x: The Bill was re-introduced in 1971, 1977, 1985, 1989, 1996, 1998, 2001, 2005 and 2008. The year 1992 was not among these years.
accepted.tq: Find the year that does not belong to a stated sequence of legislative attempts.
accepted.sec: Lokpal Bill history - first introduction, attempts, year passed, Anna Hazare movement

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Lokpal Bill passed by the Lok Sabha in 1969
B. Re-introduction of the Bill in 2008
C. Introduction of the First Lokpal Bill
D. Parliament passed the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill in December 2013
accepted.x: The correct order is introduction in 1968, passage by the Lok Sabha in 1969, re-introduction in 2008, and passage by Parliament in December 2013.
accepted.tq: Use the first and last events, then place the intermediate legislative attempt.
accepted.sec: Lokpal Bill history - first introduction, attempts, year passed, Anna Hazare movement

accepted.s:
With reference to the Lokpal Bill, 2011, consider the following statements:
1. It was introduced in the Lok Sabha in August 2011.
2. It was examined by a Standing Committee chaired by Abhishek Manu Singhvi in late 2011.
3. The new Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha on 27 December 2011.
4. The Rajya Sabha debate on the Bill was completed in December 2011 without reference to a Select Committee.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the Rajya Sabha debate remained unfinished and the Bill was sent to a Rajya Sabha Select Committee.
accepted.tq: Spot the false statement by checking the legislative procedure and its completion status.
accepted.sec: Lokpal Bill history - first introduction, attempts, year passed, Anna Hazare movement

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the sequence of parliamentary passage of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013?
o: Lok Sabha on 17 December 2013 and Rajya Sabha on 18 December 2013
Rajya Sabha on 17 December 2013 and Lok Sabha on 18 December 2013
Lok Sabha on 27 December 2011 and Rajya Sabha on 16 January 2014
accepted.x: The Rajya Sabha passed the Bill with amendments on 17 December 2013, and the Lok Sabha passed it on 18 December 2013.
accepted.tq: Read the two House dates carefully and avoid reversing the order of passage.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the dates associated with the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013?
o: Assent was given on 1 January 2014 and the Act came into force on 16 January 2014.
Assent was given on 16 January 2014 and the Act came into force on 1 January 2014.
Both assent and commencement took place on 1 January 2014.
Both assent and commencement took place on 16 January 2014.
accepted.x: The President gave assent on 1 January 2014, while the Act came into force on 16 January 2014.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two closely related dates by matching each date with its legal event.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

accepted.s: The Lokpal actually began functioning on:
accepted.x: Although the Act came into force in 2014, the Lokpal began functioning on 27 March 2019 after its Chairperson and members were appointed.
accepted.tq: Distinguish commencement of an Act from the date on which an institution began functioning.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Lokpal:
1. It is a statutory body.
2. It is a constitutional body created directly by the Constitution.
3. Its composition may include a Chairperson and up to eight members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The Lokpal is established by statute and is not a constitutional body.
accepted.tq: Use the statutory-versus-constitutional distinction and test the numerical composition separately.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

accepted.s: Which of the following is a correct feature of the composition of the Lokpal?
o: At least 75 per cent of the members must be elected MPs.
All members must be serving judges of the Supreme Court.
At least 50 per cent of the members must belong to SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities or be women.
The Chairperson and every member must be a serving MLA.
accepted.x: The Lokpal must have not less than 50 per cent representation from SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women. Its members need not all be serving judges or legislators.
accepted.tq: Test a composition requirement through the exact minimum-percentage qualification.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

accepted.s: Who among the following can be appointed as Chairperson of the Lokpal?
o: Only the serving Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Only a retired Chief Minister of a State
A former Chief Justice of India, a sitting or former Supreme Court judge, or an eminent person
Only a sitting Chief Justice of India
accepted.x: The Chairperson may be a former Chief Justice of India, a sitting or former Supreme Court judge, or an eminent person.
accepted.tq: Identify the alternatives in an eligibility list without treating one category as exclusive.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

accepted.s: Which of the following persons is NOT a member of the Selection Committee for appointment of the Lokpal?
o: Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court judge nominated by the Chief Justice of India
accepted.x: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is not a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee. The committee includes the Prime Minister, Lok Sabha Speaker, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the CJI or nominee, and an eminent jurist.
accepted.tq: Use the membership trap involving the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Selection Committee of the Lokpal:
1. The Prime Minister is its Chairperson.
2. The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha is a member.
3. One eminent jurist is nominated by the President on the recommendation of the other members.
4. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is its ex officio member.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is not a member of the Selection Committee.
accepted.tq: Identify the incorrect member by comparing the two presiding officers of Parliament.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

accepted.s:
With reference to the Search Committee constituted for the Lokpal, consider the following statements:
1. It is set up by the Selection Committee.
2. It prepares a panel for consideration.
3. It must have at least seven persons.
4. At least half of its members must be from SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Search Committee is constituted by the Selection Committee, prepares a panel, has at least seven persons and must satisfy the specified representation requirement.
accepted.tq: Check each component of a statutory committee’s constitution and functions.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the jurisdiction of the Lokpal?
o: Central officials of Groups A, B, C and D — Group C and D complaints are referred to the CVC
Members of Parliament — all speeches and votes in Parliament are subject to inquiry
NGOs — covered only when they receive foreign contribution below ₹10 lakh
Indian public servants abroad — excluded because jurisdiction ends outside India
accepted.x: The Lokpal’s jurisdiction covers central officials of Groups A, B, C and D, while complaints against Group C and D officials are sent to the CVC, which reports back to the Lokpal. Parliamentary speeches and votes are excluded, NGOs are covered above the stated threshold, and public servants outside India are included.
accepted.tq: Separate closely related jurisdictional exceptions and administrative routes.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

accepted.s: Which of the following categories of organisations comes within the Lokpal’s jurisdiction when the stated condition is fulfilled?
o: Only organisations receiving domestic donations above ₹10 lakh
Only constitutional bodies receiving no government funding
Every private company, irrespective of funding
NGOs, trusts and societies receiving foreign contributions above ₹10 lakh
accepted.x: NGOs, trusts and societies receiving foreign contributions above ₹10 lakh come within the stated jurisdiction of the Lokpal.
accepted.tq: Focus on both the organisation category and the exact monetary threshold.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

accepted.s:
The jurisdiction of the Lokpal over the Prime Minister is subject to which of the following exclusions?
1. International relations
2. Security
3. Public order
4. Atomic energy and space
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Prime Minister’s excluded areas include international relations, external and internal security, public order, atomic energy and space. Therefore, all four listed categories are covered by the exclusions.
accepted.tq: Group several statutory exceptions together and check whether any listed category falls outside them.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

accepted.s: An allegation against the Prime Minister relates to a matter not covered by the statutory exclusions. Which condition is required for an inquiry by the Lokpal?
o: Approval by the Union Cabinet through an open hearing
Prior approval of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha alone
Approval by the full Bench with at least a two-thirds majority, with the proceedings held in camera
Approval by a simple majority of any two members, in public proceedings
accepted.x: An inquiry against the Prime Minister requires approval of the full Bench by at least a two-thirds majority, and the inquiry is held in camera.
accepted.tq: Apply the special procedural safeguards to a concrete jurisdictional situation.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the jurisdiction of the Lokpal:
1. It extends to Union Ministers and Members of Parliament.
2. It covers anything said or any vote given by an MP in Parliament.
3. It applies to Indian public servants both within and outside India.
4. It covers bodies established by an Act of Parliament or funded by the government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is false because anything said or any vote given by an MP in Parliament is outside the Lokpal’s jurisdiction.
accepted.tq: Use the parliamentary speech-and-vote exception to reject an otherwise broad jurisdiction statement.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

accepted.s: A complaint is filed before the Lokpal against a Central Government employee belonging to Group D. What is the prescribed route mentioned in the Act’s working arrangement?
o: The complaint is transferred to the State Lokayukta.
The complaint goes to the Central Vigilance Commission, which reports back to the Lokpal.
The complaint is sent to the Election Commission of India.
The complaint is automatically dismissed for lack of jurisdiction.
accepted.x: Complaints against central officials in Groups C and D go to the Central Vigilance Commission, which reports back to the Lokpal.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct authority by following the special referral arrangement for lower groups of officials.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Lokpal is correct?
o: The Lokpal may inquire into a complaint filed at any time after the alleged offence.
A Chairperson or member of the Lokpal may simultaneously be an MP or MLA.
The Act applies only to public servants posted within India.
A Chairperson or member of the Lokpal cannot be an MP or MLA.
accepted.x: A Chairperson or member of the Lokpal cannot be a Member of Parliament or a Member of a Legislative Assembly. The Act also covers public servants outside India and bars complaints filed after seven years from the alleged offence.
accepted.tq: Reject the option that reverses an eligibility restriction while checking related jurisdictional limits.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

accepted.s: A complaint is made seven years after the alleged offence. Under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, the Lokpal:
o: can inquire only if the complaint concerns a Union Minister
cannot inquire into it after the statutory seven-year period
can inquire only after approval of the Rajya Sabha Chairman
must inquire into it because there is no limitation period
accepted.x: The Lokpal cannot inquire into a complaint made after seven years from the alleged offence.
accepted.tq: Apply the statutory time limit to a filing scenario.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 2016 amendment — creation of the Lokpal Selection Committee
DSPE Act amendment — abolition of the Directorate of Prosecution
2013 Act — exclusion of all Group C and D officials from every vigilance process
accepted.x: The 2016 amendment to the Lokpal law dealt with asset declarations. The Act also amended the DSPE Act in relation to the CBI Director’s committee and a Directorate of Prosecution.
accepted.tq: Match a specific amendment with its subject while rejecting broader invented consequences.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

accepted.s: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act required every State to establish a Lokayukta within:
o: Six months of the Act’s assent
Two years of the first Lokpal appointment
One year of the commencement of the Act
Five years of the establishment of the Central Vigilance Commission
accepted.x: Every State was required to set up a Lokayukta within one year of the commencement of the Act.
accepted.tq: Test the exact time limit and its starting point.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction
